sampled_review.note: No sampled review has run, so there is no pass rate. This field previously read 1.0 against n of 0, which made regression_rule.thresholds.sampled_review_pass_rate_min unable to ever fire. A null rate means the threshold is not evaluable, not that it passed.

evidence.period: 2026-08 benchmark: 45 v1 baseline runs, 45 v2 runs after the routing and oracle corrections, 18 timing-ablation runs. Testing defaults are set from the ablation: all three timings passed 6 of 6, so timing did not separate quality on these task types, but implement-then-harden cost 65 per cent more tokens and 50 per cent more wall clock than acceptance-first or alongside. Defaults therefore stay acceptance-first for gate-bearing work and alongside for ordinary features; harden-last is reserved for spikes, where deferring the oracle is the point.

authorisation_note: Authorised on 2026-08-02, one day before the benchmark it cites as evidence. The evidence block was back-filled on 2026-08-03 and the timing-ablation defaults were set from it then. The authorisation is not re-dated, because re-dating it would hide that ordering; it is recorded instead. The defaults it sets are due for reauthorisation against the rebuilt benchmark.

regression_rule.not_evaluable_reason: sampled_review.n is 0, so sampled_review_pass_rate_min has nothing to test. The rule fires on escaped_defects only until a sampled review runs.
